clue.text: Make an offer on one in the same place

indicators.note: on places the bid after the numeral, the offer sitting on top of the one

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
to bid is to make an offer, as at an auction

explanation.surface: Someone places a bid on a single item at the same venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibid is the Latin abbreviation used in footnotes to mean a source already cited just before.

clue.text: Changes relating to the whole?

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about alterations that affect everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal working on 'relating'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun in mathematics, an integral is the total sum, the complete quantity.

clue.text: Crush short protest, quietly arresting student unit

indicators.note: arresting means holding captive, so the first pair of pieces holds the next pair inside them

parts.note: demo is the short form of demonstration, a protest
sh is the call for quiet
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
I is the Roman numeral one, a unit

explanation.surface: Authorities crush a brief protest by arresting part of the student body.
explanation.definitionFit: To demolish an opponent or argument is to crush it utterly.

clue.text: Where researchers work on political party speech

parts.note: Lab is the standard abbreviation for the UK Labour Party
oratory is the art of public speaking

explanation.surface: Researchers busy themselves on a political party's speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A lab is the workplace of scientists carrying out experiments.

clue.text: Bewildered at clues, so struggle in vain

indicators.note: bewildered means confused, so these letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A solver baffled by the clues gives up on a hopeless task.
explanation.definitionFit: An effort doomed to fail is a hopeless endeavour, so a struggle in vain describes it.

clue.text: Head buzzing from a particular obsession

explanation.surface: Someone's head is buzzing because of a fixation.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally an insect buzzing under a hat on the head; figuratively a fixed preoccupation someone keeps returning to.

clue.text: One accepts child these days to choose with hesitancy

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era
to opt is to choose
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: Nowadays a prospective parent hesitates over which child to take on.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who takes a child legally into their family as their own.

clue.text: Mr Paisley supports drinks dispenser in high street outlet

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: an optic is the measuring device fixed to an upside-down bottle in a pub
Ian Paisley, the Northern Irish politician

explanation.surface: A politician props up a bar's spirit dispenser in a shopping street.
explanation.walkthrough: An OPTIC is a British pub's measure on a spirit bottle; Ian Paisley was a Northern Ireland politician and churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-test and spectacles shop is a familiar shop on a town's main shopping street.

clue.text: The call of the hills

parts.note: sounds like a phrase about longing for mountains, but means the warbling cry heard in the Alps

explanation.surface: The romantic lure of the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine herders sing in a warbling voice that switches pitch, a cry associated with mountains.

clue.text: Public service vehicles welcome quiet vagrants

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the vehicles take the quiet letter inside

parts.note: trams are public transport vehicles
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet

explanation.surface: Buses and trams quietly let homeless people aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Tramps are homeless wanderers, people with no fixed abode.

clue.text: Accompanied to secret do in disguise

indicators.note: something in disguise has its appearance altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A guest was taken along to a covert party in costume.
explanation.definitionFit: To be escorted is to be taken somewhere with a companion.

clue.text: French is limited by legal licence

indicators.note: the answer is limited by, held within, the words that follow

explanation.surface: A French claim is bounded by a legal permit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallic is an adjective for things of France, from Gaul.

clue.text: Marine teasing a lunatic

indicators.note: teasing means pulling apart, as in teasing wool, so these letters are disentangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier of the sea mocks a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: Nautical means relating to ships and the sea, as marine does.

clue.text: Waste university — and about to go back after second question

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the second and question letters
to go back means the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A complaint about university spending, raised again after a second query.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go back' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To squander money is to fritter it away, the verb sense of waste.

clue.text: Lengthened dress for elegant do

indicators.note: to dress is to arrange or prepare, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A gown let down to make it longer for a smart party.
explanation.definitionFit: Elongated means made longer, stretched out.

clue.text: Flog the tree on the left

parts.note: the ash is a common tree

explanation.surface: An order to whip the tree standing on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the left' puts L at the start of the across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash is to strike with a whip, a synonym of flog.

clue.text: Rescuing rejected student from mauling

annotationWithheld.why: Rescuing rejected student from mauling (8): SAVING round AG fits, but no standard word for student turned back gives AG, so the clue's wordplay cannot be shown honestly

clue.text: Partners' painful exclamation at fall in winter

parts.note: South and North are partners at the bridge table
ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A couple cries out in pain after a tumble in winter.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, North and South play as partners, so S and N are a crossword pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowfall is a kind of precipitation that comes down in cold weather.

clue.text: A sort of school house? Never

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
nary is an old dialect word meaning not one, never

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a house could never be a school.
explanation.walkthrough: A SEMI is a British semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college training priests, a kind of school.

clue.text: Promise pheasant and get the Scrabble!

parts.note: to give your word is to make a promise
game birds such as pheasant are called game

explanation.surface: Someone vows to shoot a pheasant and then play a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is the board game of forming words from letter tiles.

clue.text: Cops perhaps find openers on pitch

parts.note: keys are what open locks
tone is musical pitch

explanation.surface: Police uncover lock-openers on a playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: The Keystone Cops were bumbling policemen in silent film comedies; 'pitch' suggests a sports field but means a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Keystone is the film studio name attached to the famous incompetent silent-film police.

clue.text: Horsemen who jump on board

explanation.surface: Riders leap onto a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounted medieval warriors; also the chess pieces that leap over others on the chessboard.

clue.text: Playing golf in may — almost get a birdie!

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters being played with and rearranged
almost means the word may loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A golfer in springtime nearly scores a birdie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims may to MA, which joins GOLF and IN as anagram fodder; a birdie in golf is one under par, but here it is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamingo is a long-legged pink wading bird.

clue.text: One is ruffled by father being sick

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest
ill means being sick

explanation.surface: Someone is upset by their father's illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A frill is a gathered or pleated strip of fabric, a ruffle.

clue.text: Complained about network boxing exercises

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the network word encloses the exercises

parts.note: a grid is a network of lines
PE is physical education, exercises at school

explanation.surface: Someone grumbled about a network running boxing workouts.
explanation.definitionFit: To gripe is to grumble or moan.

clue.text: National hotel accepted by girl crew

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so the girl and crew pieces enclose the hotel letter

parts.note: Iris is a girl's name
to man a ship is to crew it
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel takes on a girl as crew.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irishman is a person of the Irish nation, a national of Ireland.

clue.text: Shock university degree on art work

indicators.note: on places the university and degree pieces after the reworked art
work suggests the letters of art being worked into a new shape

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A university degree in art turns out to be a shock.
explanation.definitionFit: Trauma is emotional or physical shock.

clue.text: One harshly criticised after support is made legal

indicators.note: after places the one and criticised pieces behind the support

parts.note: a leg supports a table
I is the Roman numeral one
slated means heavily criticised

explanation.surface: A person panned by critics is backed and then made lawful.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make law, so what is legislated has been passed into law.

clue.text: College porter on the fourth of July?

indicators.note: on the places the beer after the letter taken from July
fourth of picks the fourth letter of the word July

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, a type of ale

explanation.surface: A college doorman on Independence Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' suggests a college doorman but is the beer; the Fourth of July is US Independence Day, apt for an American college.
explanation.definitionFit: Yale is an Ivy League university in Connecticut.
